html:
The Yankunytjatjara are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northwest of South Australia, in the desert country south and east of Uluru. The map shows them as Yankuntjatjara from 1600 to 1815. They speak a dialect of the Western Desert language and belong to the Western Desert cultural bloc.

With their close kin the Pitjantjatjara, they call themselves Anangu. Other neighbours were the Antakirinja to the southeast and the Luritja to the north.

In 1953 a British atomic test at Emu Field, part of the British nuclear tests in South Australia, sent a black cloud over Yankunytjatjara camps. Many fell sick. A boy at one of the camps, Yami Lester, later went blind and became a leading campaigner. In 1981 South Australia gave the Anangu freehold title to a large block of their country, and in 1985 Uluru was handed back to its Anangu owners.
